title: Review: static-analysis deviance evidence set (26 MISRA deviation records)
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft' rather than 'reviewed' or 'approved': this record is the output of an automated review pass and no human reviewer has confirmed it. automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation only and is not a statement about engineering validity.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Domain review of the 26 as_is deviation records against the real foxBMS 2 source at the pinned baseline commit 308028fb.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 this is an automated review: it is NOT organizational independence, NOT human confirmation, and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, independent party, or separate agent session participated.

scope: Full scope over all 26 as_is deviation records (FB2-SW-DEV-000001..000026). Every deviations entry in every record was checked against the real source file named by affected_file. All 26 records carry profile 'as_is', so every reviewed_id below resolves unambiguously in the as_is profile.

findings.description: Record FB2-SW-DEV-000001 correctly declares its third deviations entry as suppression_form 'next_codeline' at lines 680-681 and annotates it as outside the 43-hit literal query while belonging to the same symbol and rule. A naive checker that requires every affected_lines range to be a Disable/Enable block pair will report this entry as a mismatch. This is a property of the checker, not a defect in the record; recorded so a later reviewer does not mistake a correct record for a wrong one.
findings.evidence: src/app/application/redundancy/redundancy.c:680 is '/* AXIVION Next Codeline Style MisraC2012Directive-4.1: truncation impossible;' and :681 is the continuation line 'we sum INT32 values x times and divide by x, resulting in INT32'. The record's deviations[2] carries suppression_form 'next_codeline' and an explanatory note.

findings.description: The corpus_scope scope_note states that all 43 'AXIVION Disable Style MisraC2012*' lines under src/ are represented. Verified true. Two further affected_lines starts lie outside that literal query - src/app/main/include/general.h:108 and redundancy.c:680 - and both are already documented in their own record with a note explaining the exclusion. The coverage claim is therefore accurate and the exclusions are visible, not silent.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'AXIVION Disable Style MisraC2012' src/ returns exactly 43 lines across 20 files; every one is the start of a deviations entry. The only two non-matching affected_lines starts are general.h:108 ('AXIVION Disable Style Generic-NoUnsafeMacro MisraC2012Directive-4.9') and redundancy.c:680, both explained in-record.

dispositions.action: No record change required. The entry is correct as written. Any future automated deviation checker must branch on the declared suppression_form before asserting a Disable/Enable block pair; this review records the case so the checker is not written against a wrong assumption.
No record change required. Coverage claim confirmed by independent enumeration; the two out-of-query sites remain visible through their in-record notes.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organizational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9).
human_approval_status is 'pending' for every artifact covered by this review. No human reviewer signed any of them.
No artifact covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit.

Scope is the 26 as_is deviation records only. Axivion annotations outside the mined query (for example 'AXIVION Routine MisraC2012Directive-4.1', 'Next Codeline Generic-*' and 'CodingStyle-Naming.*') were NOT reviewed; their absence from this review is not evidence that no further deviation exists.

No claim is made about the engineering acceptability of any deviation. This review verifies source-grounding and honesty of the anti-conformance fields only. It does not assess whether any waived MISRA C:2012 rule leaves unacceptable residual risk, and it does not assert any ISO 26262 safety classification.

The Axivion tool was not re-run and no static analysis was performed. No tool qualification or checker qualification is claimed; the repository classifies no static-analysis tool in docs/developer-manual/software/criticality-mapping-of-third-party-tools.csv.

Verification performed: (a) all 36 deviations entries checked for Disable-at-range-start, Enable-at-range-end and rule identifier on both annotations; (b) corpus_scope hit_count recomputed from the source tree; (c) all 26 source anchors resolved against docs/artifacts/sources/source-registry.json; (d) all 26 anchor content_hash values recomputed as sha256 of the referenced file's current bytes and matched; (e) no file drift between pinned commit 308028fb, HEAD (c29b829c) and the working tree.
Of those checks, (a) is qualified by the one correctly-declared next_codeline entry (FB2-REV-FND-000101); (b) through (e) were clean for all 26 records with no exceptions.
review_method: Direct source inspection. For each record the named source file was read, every AXIVION annotation line enumerated with its line number, and each affected_lines range compared against the Disable and Enable annotation actually present at those lines. Anchor content hashes were recomputed from file bytes and cross-checked against the pinned commit via git show, read-only.
